title: WPSS/627/2015 of Prakash Bhatt AND OTHERS Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
WPSS No. 627 of 2015
Honíble Rajiv Sharma, J.
Mr. Vinay Kumar, Advocate for the
petitioners.
Mr. Vikas Pande, Standing Counsel, for
the State.
Mr. N.S. Pundir, Advocate, for the
respondent no.3.
Ms. Sonia Chawla, Advocate holding
brief of Mr. Paresh Tripathi, Advocate, for the
respondent no.4.
Mr. Manoj Tiwari, Sr. Advocate,
Advocate for the respondent no.6.
Applications were invited vide
advertisement dated 4.5.2011 for filling up 85
posts of Assistant Agriculture Officer Grade-I
(Development Branch). Petitioners also
participated in the selection process. The
written examination was held on 25.9.2011.
The last candidate in the general merit has
secured 45% marks and in the S.C. category,
the last selected candidate has secured
33.75% marks.
Case of the petitioners, in a nutshell, is
that the Selection Committee was required to
prepare the panel as per Rule 15(4) of the
Uttar Pradesh Subordinate Agriculture Service
Rules, 1993.
The State Government has filed its reply.
It is stated in the reply that vide letters dated
21.5.2012, 4.6.2012, 13.8.2012 and
28.9.2012, the Agriculture Directorate has
asked the Secretary, Uttarakhand Technical
Education Board, Roorkee, Haridwar to send
the names of 6 selected candidates for 4 posts
of Assistant Agriculture, Grade-I,
Development Branch and 2 posts for
Chemistry Branch. It was further apprised
that out of total 85 selected candidates, 3
women and 1 General Category (male) for
Development Branch and 17 selected
candidates in Chemistry Branch, 2 male
(General) have not given their joining.
According to the petitioners, 4 posts are
still lying vacant. The Technical Board, in its
reply, has also admitted this position.
However, the ground taken by the respondent-

State to deny the appointment to the
petitioners is that as per letter dated
26.8.2005, a ban has been imposed for
preparing the merit list by panel.
Letter dated 26.8.2005 is on record as
Annexure No.CA3 to the reply filed by the
State. Letter dated 26.8.2005 could not
substitute the Recruitment & Promotion
Rules, as noticed hereinabove. The
departmental instructions/memorandum can
only supplement but the same cannot
supplant the Rules. According to Rule 15(4)
of the Rules, a Panel was required to be
prepared and the Department was also aware
of this position. Thus, the letters dated
21.5.2012, 4.6.2012, 13.8.2012 and
28.9.2012 were sent by the Department to the
Secretary, Technical Education Board,
Roorkee, Haridwar.
Petitioner nos.1 and 2 have obtained
41.5 and 40 marks whereas, petitioner no.3,
who belongs to S.C. category, has secured
32.75 marks. Petitioners were immediately
below the last selected candidates in the
general category as well as in S.C. category.
The Selection Board/Committee was required
to prepare the Panel as per the Rules, noticed
hereinabove, and the Technical Board was
also required to recommend the names for
appointment of petitioners and similarly
situate persons after the selected candidates
had not submitted their joining. The action of
the respondents not to offer appointment to
the petitioners and similarly situate persons,
who are though qualified, even after the
availability of vacancies as per advertisement
dated 4.5.2011, is arbitrary, discriminatory,
unreasonable and thus, violative of Articles 14
and 16 of the Constitution of India. The
appointing authority can refuse the
appointment but on plausible and cogent
reason alone.
It is not one of those cases where the
candidates have joined and subsequently
resigned, but here, the selected candidates
have not joined at all. Thus, as many as 04
clear cut vacancies are available and were
required to be offered to the petitioner and

similarly situate persons. In (2013) 12 SCC
Page 171, their Lordships of Hon. Supreme
Court in the case of ëManoj Manu & another v.
Union of India & othersí have held that non-forwarding of names from reserve/waiting list
may not be justified, especially when there is
a specific requisition by the appointment
authority therefor. In paragraph no.9, their
Lordships have held as under: -
ì9. It can be clearly inferred from the reading of the
aforesaid that it is not the case where any of these
persons initially joined as Section Officer and thereafter
resigned/left/promoted, etc. thereby creating the
vacancies again. Had that been the situation viz. after
the vacancy had been filled up, and caused again
because of some subsequent event, position would have
been different. In that eventuality UPSC would be right
in not forwarding the names from the list as there is
culmination of the process with the exhaustion of the
notified vacancies and vacancies arising thereafter have
to be filled up by fresh examination. However, in the
instant case, out of 184 persons recommended, six
persons did not join at all. In these circumstances when
the candidates in reserved list on the basis of
examination already held, were available and DoPT had
approached UPSC ìwithin a reasonable timeî to send the
names, we do not see any reason or justification on the
part of UPSC not to send the names.î
Accordingly, the writ petition is allowed.
The respondents are directed to consider the
case of petitioners for appointment to the post
of Assistant Agriculture Officer Grade-I
(Development Branch, against the available
vacancies, within a period of four weeks from
today.
All pending applications stand
disposed of.
